about: The price anomaly rules. scripts/price_anomalies.py reads this file (its CLI defaults come from it), so change a threshold or field list here and nowhere else. Each key is explained under notes.

notes.price_fields: Product attributes read as the shelf price, first present wins. When a regular_price_fields attribute is also present, this is treated as the current (possibly discounted) price.
notes.sale_price_fields: Product attributes read as the sale price, first present wins (Discovery feeds use sale_price).
notes.regular_price_fields: Attributes that hold the regular (before-discount) price. Engagement catalogs often have price plus original_price: original_price is then the regular price and price the current one.
notes.variant_price_fields: Variant attributes read as the variant's regular price (the grid's inline variants use sku_price).
notes.variant_sale_price_fields: Variant attributes read as the variant's sale price.
notes.group_fields: Attributes used to group products for the like-for-like comparison, first present wins. A LABEL=FILE input overrides them with the label, for files fetched one category at a time.
notes.group_value_separators: A group value holding several values joined by one of these keeps only the first, so 'Cutting Boards|Cheese Boards' groups under 'Cutting Boards'.
notes.group_path_separators: A group value that is a breadcrumb path is split on these, so 'Home > Kitchen > Knives' is the path Home, Kitchen, Knives.
notes.group_level: Which level of a breadcrumb path to group by: 'leaf' (the last segment, default: 'Home > Kitchen > Knives' groups under Knives, like for like) or 'top' (the first segment: whole departments).
notes.title_fields: Attributes read as the product title (shown in findings and used for the near-identical title check).
notes.brand_fields: Attributes read as the brand (the near-identical title check only compares products of the same brand).
notes.id_fields: Attributes read as the product ID, first present wins.
notes.views_fields: Performance table columns read as views, first present wins.
notes.min_group_size: A group needs at least this many priced products before its outliers and unit errors are judged; smaller groups are listed under not_checked.
notes.robust_z: A price is an outlier when its distance from the group median, on a log scale, is more than this many robust standard deviations (1.4826 x the median absolute deviation). 3.5 is the usual modified z-score cut-off.
notes.min_ratio: An outlier must also be at least this many times above the group median, or this many times below it, so tight groups don't flag ordinary prices. When the median absolute deviation is 0 (most of the group shares one price), this ratio alone decides.
notes.unit_factors: Factors checked for unit or decimal errors. An outlier is a likely unit error when its price divided (or multiplied) by one of these lands inside the group's typical range.
notes.typical_band: The group's typical range is its lower to upper quartile, widened by this factor each way (Q1 / band to Q3 x band).
notes.max_discount: A sale price more than this share below the regular price (0.8 = over 80% off) is reported as a discount beyond the sane maximum.
notes.sale_equal_default_share: When at least this share of priced products have a sale price equal to the regular price, the feed is filling sale_price by default: it's reported once as a catalog note, not per product.
notes.variant_spread_ratio: Variants of one product whose highest price is at least this many times the lowest are reported.
notes.duplicate_price_tolerance: The same product ID, or the same brand and title after folding, at prices more than this share apart is reported (0.05 = 5%).
notes.min_views: A product with at least this many views (from the performance table) counts as exposed, as does any revenue or a page-one position on a top query.
notes.page_size: A product at or above this position in a saved --rank grid is on page one.
notes.top_queries: How many of the highest-revenue queries to save page one for, for the exposure ranking. Read by the SKILL.md call plan, not the script.
notes.max_findings_listed: At most this many findings are listed in full in the JSON output, highest priority and exposure first; the rest are counted and all of them go to --csv.
notes.never_output_fields: Commercial fields the script never reads or outputs, even when the catalog has them. Also don't ask for them in the grid's fl.
